about: Behaviour resin is known to get wrong, approximate or refuse. Each entry has a repro in tests/unit/known_gaps.test.ts. 'it.fails' repros assert the CORRECT behaviour and are expected to fail today: when a gap is closed its test starts passing, which fails the suite and forces the entry to be removed. 'warned' repros assert that transpile() reports it. 'pinned' repros assert today's (loud) refusal. tvVerified is false everywhere: this file's expectations come from arithmetic, the repo's own documentation or the Pine reference's definitions, not from a TradingView run, and an entry says so in 'expectation'.

gaps.title: request.security on the chart's own bars delivers a higher-timeframe value one chart bar late
gaps.expectation: The same bars passed as a feed (run option `security`) pair correctly; building the higher timeframe from the chart's bars must give the same values. README documents the lag.

gaps.title: request.security on a named symbol with no feed reads the chart's own bars
gaps.expectation: A run warning says so (RunResult.warnings); refusing is still open.

gaps.title: hour, dayofweek and the other time builtins read UTC even when syminfo.timezone is set
gaps.expectation: With timezone Asia/Seoul (UTC+9, no DST) `hour` is the UTC hour + 9. UNVERIFIED against TradingView: src/runtime/datetime.ts suspects it; README and API.md document the UTC reading.

gaps.title: An unknown timezone string passed to a time builtin is read as UTC
gaps.expectation: hour(time, "Mars/Phobos") is refused (at transpile time or by a typed runtime error).

gaps.title: An unparsable timeframe literal in request.security is read as the daily timeframe
gaps.expectation: request.security(…, "garbage", …) is refused at transpile time.

gaps.title: time_close is the next bar's open time, so it is wrong across a gap in the data
gaps.expectation: On a 60-minute chart time_close - time is one hour for every bar, including the bar before a gap.

gaps.title: matrix.eigenvalues returns the diagonal for matrices larger than 2x2
gaps.expectation: The eigenvalues of [[2,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,4]] are 3 - sqrt(3), 3, 3 + sqrt(3) (arithmetic).

gaps.title: ta.correlation returns exactly 0 for series at a very small price level
gaps.expectation: Correlation is scale-invariant: the same data multiplied by 1e-6 gives the same coefficients. src/runtime/ta.ts treats a covariance under 1e-10 as zero, which may be a deliberate port of Pine's comparison tolerance.

gaps.title: ta.bbw is 100 times the width ratio, while ta.kcw (corrected against TradingView in 0.3.0) is the plain ratio
gaps.expectation: ta.bbw(close, 20, 2) equals (upper - lower) / basis from ta.bb. UNVERIFIED against TradingView: the only evidence for the x100 is a pine2py golden that has not changed since 0.1.0.

gaps.title: Drawing ids come from a process-global counter, so two runs in one process differ
gaps.expectation: Running the same script twice gives an identical RunResult.viz.

gaps.title: line.all, label.all, box.all (and the other drawing collections) are always empty
gaps.expectation: After creating two lines, array.size(line.all) is 2.

gaps.title: request.dividends, splits, earnings, quandl, financial, seed and currency_rate return placeholders
gaps.expectation: Reported as `stub` warnings; refused under `strict`.

gaps.title: ticker.heikinashi, renko, kagi, linebreak and pointfigure return their symbol unchanged
gaps.expectation: Reported as `passthrough` warnings; refused under `strict`.

gaps.title: request.security_lower_tf returns a one-element array holding the chart bar's own value
gaps.expectation: Reported as a `stub` warning; refused under `strict`.

gaps.title: strategy.risk.* rules are implemented from the function names and only block new entries
gaps.expectation: Reported as a `hypothesis` warning.

gaps.title: strategy() parameters close_entries_rule and backtest_fill_limits_assumption are accepted and never read
gaps.expectation: A value other than the default that resin implements is reported as a `stub` warning; refused under `strict`.

gaps.title: 16 ta.* functions (ema, rsi, rma, atr, alma, hma, dema, cog, ...) refuse a length that changes from bar to bar
gaps.expectation: Today's refusal. When a function learns to take a series length its entry here must be edited, not deleted.

gaps.title: Grammar errors resin accepts: reserved words as names, missing commas in parameter/tuple/generic lists, junk after a declaration
gaps.expectation: Each script in tests/negative/false_accepts.json (category grammar) is refused. They are invalid under any reading of the grammar; the parser is lenient where pine2py was.

gaps.title: A declaration with a type name that is declared nowhere is accepted
gaps.expectation: `foo x = 1`, `flaot x = 1.0`, `let x = 1` are refused (category undeclared-type).

gaps.title: There is no static type checker beyond literals: ill-typed scripts compile and misbehave at run time
gaps.expectation: `int x = "a"`, `"a" * 2`, `plot("a")`, `ta.sma(close, "5")` are refused (category static-type). A checker has to be validated against the Pine reference before it may refuse real scripts. Since src/transpiler/types/check.ts the errors visible on literals (16 of the 19) are a `type` warning and refused under `strict`; by default they are still accepted, and anything whose type must be inferred is not judged.

gaps.title: Some builtins are accepted with fewer arguments than their Pine signature has required parameters
gaps.expectation: `label.new()`, `line.new(1)`, `alert()` are refused (category builtin-arity). Since the signature table (src/transpiler/builtins/signatures.ts, generated from the oracle's library) the ones it describes are a `signature` warning and refused under `strict`; by default they are still accepted, and `alert()` and `timeframe.change()` are not described by the table.

gaps.title: One NaN, Infinity or out-of-range bar time makes any script that reads the exchange calendar throw a raw RangeError, and the run's warnings are lost with it
gaps.expectation: The run completes and RunResult.warnings names the bad bar (found by scripts/fuzz.mjs, KD8 in tests/robustness/README.md).

gaps.title: A strategy with percent commission throws SyntaxError (a BigInt conversion of NaN) when the bar an order fills on has a NaN open
gaps.expectation: The run completes (an order with no fill price is not filled, or the data hole is reported); KD9 in tests/robustness/README.md.

gaps.title: Extreme values reach the host as raw RangeErrors: str.format_time past JavaScript's Date range, a string that doubles every bar
gaps.expectation: Today's behaviour: a RangeError, not a typed error and not an abort (KD4, KD7 in tests/robustness/README.md).

gaps.title: str.match runs the script's pattern as an unbounded JavaScript RegExp: nested quantifiers on a 45-character string never return
gaps.expectation: Checked in a child process by tests/robustness/fuzz_cli.test.ts (KD11); no host limit covers it, a host that needs a hard bound runs the engine in a worker it can terminate.

gaps.title: ta.roc with a series length takes its numerator over the non-na bars only, so across an na gap it differs from the same call with a literal length
gaps.expectation: Found by tests/property: close = [10, 11, na, 13, 14], ta.roc(close, 2) is 18.18 at bar 3 but ta.roc(close, 2 + bar_index * 0) is 27.27. src/runtime/ta.ts rocVarLen says that is 'as the oracle runs it', so it may be TradingView's behaviour; the two literal/series forms agreeing is the property that fails.
